name: Katherine V. Forrest
knownFor: Author of Curious Wine and the Kate Delafield mysteries; "a founding mother of lesbian fiction".
bio: Katherine V. Forrest was born in Windsor, Ontario, and is a Canadian-born American writer. She is best known for her nine novels about Kate Delafield, a Los Angeles homicide detective who was the first lesbian police detective in American lesbian mystery fiction, and for the romance Curious Wine, a classic of American lesbian literature.

She was for ten years fiction editor at Naiad Press, later founded and became supervising editor at Spinsters Ink, and has edited many anthologies of lesbian and gay interest. Her books have won, or been finalists for, the Lambda Literary Award twelve times.

events.text: Published Curious Wine with Naiad Press.
Published the first Kate Delafield mystery, Amateur City, and the science-fiction novel Daughters of a Coral Dawn.
Received the Lambda Literary Foundation's Pioneer Award.
Received the Alice B Readers Award.
Received the Golden Crown Literary Society's Trailblazer Award and the Bill Whitehead Award for Lifetime Achievement from Publishing Triangle.

relevance: Curious Wine was one of the first lesbian romances to treat its heroines as women with every option who chose the hardest one — to love each other — and it is credited with breaking through many misconceptions about lesbians and their relationships. She is also noted for the open treatment of sexuality in her work.
influence: As an editor she worked with hundreds of writers, among them Jane Rule and Lee Lynch, and as a founding editor at Naiad and Spinsters Ink she helped build the independent presses that made the genre.
